messages.content: Can you use the 'update_user_info' function to update the name and email of a customer with user ID 12345 in the 'CustomerInfo' database to "John" and "example@.com", then repeat the same process for another customer with user ID 67890, changing their name and email to the same value as well as well?

function.name: update_user_info
function.description: Update user information in the database. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_id.description: The user ID of the customer.

database.description: The database where the user's information is stored.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to call the function twice. They want to update user ID 12345 to name "John" and email "example@.com". Then repeat for user ID 67890 with same values. We need to call the function twice. The function signature: update_user_info takes user_id (number), update_info (object with optional name, email), database (string). The default database is "CustomerInfo". So we can omit database or specify it.

We should produce two calls. According to guidelines, we should not provide a single combined request; we need separate calls. The user says "then repeat the same process for another customer with user ID 67890, changing their name and email to the same value as well as well?" That seems like they want to do the same update for both customers. So we will call the function twice.

We need to output JSON calls. The format: {"name":"function_name","arguments":{...}}. For each call. We can output them sequentially. The assistant should respond with the calls. There's no mention of needing to handle errors. We'll just call the function.

We need to ensure we don't include any extraneous text. Just the calls. The user didn't ask for anything else. So we output:

{"name":"functions.update_user_info","arguments":{"user_id":12345,"update_info":{"name":"John","email":"example@.com"}}}
{"name":"functions.update_user_info","arguments":{"user_id":67890,"update_info":{"name":"John","email":"example@.com"}}}

We might also include database if needed. But default is CustomerInfo. It's fine to omit. The user said "in the 'CustomerInfo' database". The default is that. So it's okay.

Thus we output two calls.
